Distinguish this project from a DIFFERENT, larger, ultimately-SHELVED 2014-2017 Vector bidirectional-flow/capacity-doubling proposal (Oil & Gas Journal 2014-10-08, 'Vector Pipeline floats doubling capacity, bidirectional flow'; Detroit Free Press 2015-02-03, 'Vector shelves pipeline expansion') -- that project targeted ~650,000 Mcfd of NEW bidirectional capacity for a 2017 in-service and was abandoned; it is unrelated to the smaller, completed 2019-2021 Bluewater Compression Project this row records, though the OGJ article does independently place 'Blue Water Gas Storage (Lenox, Michigan)' -- Lenox Township is in Macomb County -- as an existing Vector interconnect, corroborating the Michigan location. validity.recommendation: Change EndState/Province from 'Wisconsin' to 'Michigan' -- the project is a compressor station located entirely in Macomb County, Michigan, not a route that terminates in Wisconsin.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's EndState/Province='Wisconsin' does not match any independent source. Four independent sources agree the compressor station and its interconnect are entirely within Michigan and that Vector Pipeline itself never reaches Wisconsin: (1) EIA workbook, this exact project row: Beg_State=MI, End_State=MI, Crosses State Border='No'; (2) Gas Compression Magazine: 'a new compressor station in Macomb County, Michigan, USA'; (3) Enbridge's own factsheet (Aug. 2023; the sheet's own harvested citation): Vector Pipeline runs 'between Joliet, IL and Dawn, ON' with interconnections 'located in Michigan, Indiana, Illinois, and Ontario' -- Wisconsin appears only once, as a MARKET reachable through those interconnections ('flow gas ... to markets located throughout the Midwest (MI, IN, IL and WI)'), never as a physical terminus; (4) offshore-technology.com and (5) Wikipedia's Vector Pipeline article both independently give the same Illinois-to-Ontario route via Indiana/Michigan, with zero mention of Wisconsin as an endpoint. Likely origin of the error: Bluewater Gas Storage LLC (the compressor project's owner/operator -- see the Owner concern below) is itself a subsidiary of WEC Energy Group, whose Wisconsin utility subsidiaries We Energies and Wisconsin Public Service are named on bluewatergasstorage.com as the customers this storage facility ultimately serves ('seasonal storage needs for 1.5 million natural gas customers of We Energies and Wisconsin Public Service') -- Wisconsin is where the gas is ultimately consumed, not where this pipe/compressor sits. StartState/Province='Michigan' is correct and needs no change.

Every source that names a company for the Bluewater Compression Project names 'Bluewater Gas Storage LLC', not Enbridge or DTE: the EIA workbook's Pipeline Operator Name field for this exact row is 'Bluewater Gas Storage'; Gas Compression Magazine names 'Bluewater Gas Storage LLC's (Bluewater) Bluewater Compression Project' as the FERC applicant, builder and owner of the new compressor station. Independently, WEC Energy Group's own corporate website (wecenergygroup.com) lists 'Bluewater Gas Storage' under its Subsidiaries, and bluewatergasstorage.com's own footer/branding confirms the WEC Energy Group affiliation -- neither page mentions Enbridge or DTE Energy at all. Enbridge's own factsheet, which itemizes Enbridge's actual gas-storage/transmission joint ventures in the St. Clair, Ontario area (a DIFFERENT, similarly-named 'Bluewater Pipeline' owned by St. Clair Pipelines L.P., 1.8 miles in Lambton County, Ontario -- not to be confused with this Michigan project), never mentions Bluewater Gas Storage LLC or this Macomb County compressor station as an Enbridge/DTE asset. Ownership percentage for Bluewater Gas Storage LLC itself (wholly WEC-owned vs. a JV) was not stated explicitly by any source opened this session, so Owner1% is left for the researcher to source rather than guessed; Owner2 candidate is left blank ('') since no second owner was identified.
